settings.description: Name players see in the in-game browser. A name given on the launch line replaces this one.
Welcome text shown to players on login. A literal backslash-n in the value becomes a line break.
How many seconds the message of the day stays on screen after a player joins.
Password players must type to join. Leave it blank for an open server; it cannot hold a question mark or the launch chain breaks.
Separate password that lets a non-admin enter spectator mode to watch the server.
TCP port of the remote console the Dialwarden hooks use. A value on the launch line takes priority over this one.
Turns on the remote console. The save, chat and clean-exit hooks all depend on it.
How many recent game-log lines the server keeps for remote console clients to fetch.
Unlocks admin commands and is also the remote console login. Use a long secret without spaces or question marks.
Copies admin command use into the chat log so players can see what admins did.
Idle time before a player is kicked. Only applies when the server runs with the idle-kick launch flag.
Minutes between automatic world saves. Very short intervals cause noticeable hitches.
Scales experience from every source, for survivors, tribes and tamed creatures alike.
Speeds up taming progress. A value of 2 roughly halves the time a tame takes.
Overall speed of in-game time. Values above 1 make each full day pass faster.
Extra scaling applied only to experience earned from kills, on top of the global rate.
Extra scaling applied only to experience earned from gathering resources.
Extra scaling applied only to experience earned from crafting items.
Replaces the survivor experience cap. Zero keeps the built-in cap; a custom level ramp is usually needed too.
Scales the wait between feedings on passive tames. Lower values let players feed sooner.
How many resources each gathering hit gives, for both survivors and creatures.
Toughness of trees, rocks and bushes. Higher values let each node take more hits.
Regrowth delay for harvested nodes. Lower values bring them back sooner.
Damage survivors deal to resource nodes, which changes how fast a node is used up.
Damage creatures deal to resource nodes. The shipped value is 3.2, not 1.
Limits harvest damage to the health left in the node, which curbs extreme yields from strong tames.
How quickly seeds in crop plots grow into harvestable plants.
Scales all damage that survivors deal, with weapons or with their fists.
Scales damage survivors receive. Values below 1 make them harder to kill.
How fast survivors get hungry. Lower values mean eating less often.
How fast survivors get thirsty. Lower values mean drinking less often.
Stamina cost of sprinting, jumping, swimming and melee for survivors.
Speed at which survivors regain health over time on their own.
Lets survivors reset their stat points with a respec potion without waiting for the cooldown.
Scales the starting value of a survivor stat. The index picks the stat; index 0 is health.
Scales damage dealt by every creature, wild or tamed, to any target.
Scales damage creatures receive. Values below 1 make them tougher in fights.
Hunger speed for creatures. It also changes how fast unconscious tames burn through food.
Extra hunger scaling for tamed creatures only, applied on top of the general food drain.
Total number of tamed creatures allowed on the whole server before taming is refused.
Per-tribe tame limit. Zero means no per-tribe limit; only the server-wide one applies.
Density of wild creature spawns. High values cost a lot of server CPU and memory.
Allows putting level-up points into movement speed on ground creatures.
Allows putting level-up points into movement speed on flying creatures.
On PvE servers, lets flying tames pick up and carry other players and creatures.
Cooldown before a female can mate again. Lower values shorten the wait.
How quickly fertilized eggs incubate and gestation finishes. Higher values are faster.
Time between unfertilized egg drops. Lower values mean more eggs for kibble.
How quickly babies grow to adulthood. Imprint timing scales along with it.
How fast babies eat. Lower values make raising them easier to keep up with.
Time between imprint care requests. Lower values bring more frequent requests, each worth more.
Size of the stat bonus a fully imprinted creature gets. Zero removes the bonus.
Imprint percentage gained from each completed care request.
Lets any tribe member do the imprint care, not only the player who claimed the baby.
Removes the extra damage and resistance a rider gets on a creature they imprinted.
Scales damage buildings receive. Values below 1 make bases harder to break.
Scales damage dealt by structures such as turrets and spike walls.
Most building pieces allowed in one local area. It limits base sprawl and lag.
Scales how many pieces fit on platform saddles and rafts.
Hard cap on building pieces on a single platform saddle.
Allows turrets and other normally blocked structures to be placed on platform saddles.
Lets players pick structures back up at any time, not just shortly after placing them.
Window after placing a structure during which it can still be picked up.
Allows building pieces to be placed even when they would clip into terrain or objects.
Turns the server into PvE: players cannot damage players, tames or bases of other tribes.
Hardcore mode: a dead survivor starts over from level 1 with a new character.
Shields the base of a tribe once all members have logged off, after the configured delay.
Delay after the last tribe member logs off before offline raid protection starts.
Stops tribe members and their tames from hurting each other on PvP servers.
Same protection against hurting your own tribe, applied on PvE servers.
On PvE, lets two tribes agree to a timed war during which they can fight each other.
Adds a growing respawn delay for players killed again and again in PvP.
Lets survivors switch to an over-the-shoulder camera on foot.
Shows the aiming crosshair for players. Turn it off for a harder shooting experience.
Marks the position of each player on their own map screen.
Largest allowed tribe size. Zero means no limit; 1 makes everyone play solo.
Stops abandoned buildings on PvE from becoming claimable or removed over time.
Stops tames of inactive PvE players from becoming claimable by others over time.
Scales how long PvE buildings last without their owner. Higher values keep them longer.
Scales how long PvE tames stay protected while their owner is inactive.
Turns on the abandoned-building timer on PvP servers, using the PvE decay periods.
Turns on the abandoned-tame timer on PvP servers, so tames of inactive tribes expire.
Removes buildings left alone for long enough. Zero turns this cleanup off completely.
Shelf life of perishable items. Higher values make food and meat last longer.
How long bodies stay in the world before vanishing, including the body of the player.
Stops players bringing in characters uploaded on another server. Belongs in the server settings; the client section copy has no effect.
Stops players taking items out of the transfer storage on this server.
Stops players taking creatures out of the transfer storage on this server.
Stops characters from leaving this server for other servers.
Stops players putting items into transfer storage from this server.
Stops players putting creatures into transfer storage from this server.
How many creatures one player can hold in transfer storage at once.
How many item stacks one player can hold in transfer storage at once.
Scales how many of one item fit into a single inventory slot.
Raises or lowers the quality of gear found in supply drops and loot crates.
Raises or lowers the quality of items pulled up with a fishing rod.
How strongly the crafting skill of a survivor improves the quality of crafted gear.
Lets players write their own cooking recipes for meals and drinks.
Gives every survivor all crafting recipes straight away, with no engram points needed.
Stops supply drops and loot crates from spawning anywhere on the map.
Health a survivor gains for each point spent on level-up.
Carry weight a survivor gains for each point spent on level-up.
Melee damage a survivor gains for each point spent on level-up.
Health that wild creatures roll for each level they spawn with.
Health a tame gains for each point spent after taming. The built-in value is 0.2, not 1.
Melee damage a tame gains for each point spent after taming. The built-in value is 0.17.
Flat health bonus a creature gets at the moment it is tamed. The built-in value is 0.14.
Extra health from taming effectiveness, so better tames get more. The built-in value is 0.44.
Sets difficulty directly; the top wild level is 30 times this value. Zero means unused; 5 gives level 150 creatures.
Older difficulty slider within the base range of the map. It mostly stops mattering once the override is set.
Applies the solo-play balance (faster taming, breeding and more) to a dedicated server.
Shows a beam of light where a player died so they can find their gear again.
Turns off illnesses that survivors can otherwise catch, such as swamp fever.
Wipes and respawns all wild creatures at this interval on restart. Zero turns it off.
Cryopods keep their creature safe without having to be stored in a cryofridge.
Older slot limit. Hosting tools report that the server ignores it; keep it equal to the launch flag.
Server name on the travel chain. It must not contain a question mark or quotes; quote the whole chain when it has spaces.
UDP game port players connect to. Use the dash form; the question-mark form is handled inconsistently by tools.
The game port written as a question-mark option. The server best follows the dash form, so remove this one.
Player slot limit the server actually honours. Set the cap here, not in the INI.
Remote console port given on the travel chain. One tool measured that an INI-only value was ignored, so keep this in line with the INI.
Launch-line switch for the remote console. When present it replaces the INI setting.
Admin password on the travel chain. It must be the last question-mark option: everything after it is read as part of the password.
Binds the server to one local IP address on hosts with several network interfaces.
Starts the server without the anti-cheat. Some launchers pass the opposite switch instead.
Writes admin and gameplay events to a separate server log that remote console clients can also read.
Save layout where player and tribe data live inside the map save; needed for some hosted-save imports.
Shared id that links servers for travel. Use a random private string, never the word default.
Folder holding transfer data. Every server in the cluster must point to the same path.
Blocks characters and items arriving from servers outside your own cluster id.
Lets players fly creatures inside caves, which is normally blocked on most maps.
Turns on a seasonal event by its internal name. Leave empty for no event.
Which client platforms may join: PC, XSX, PS5, WINGDK or ALL, combined with plus signs.
Comma-separated CurseForge project ids. The server downloads and loads them at boot.
Mod ids kept loaded so their saved data survives, but not active in gameplay.

rules.message: The game port is given as a question-mark option; write it as -Port= instead, which every tool reads.
The remote console is on but there is no admin password, so it cannot log in and the save, chat and exit hooks fail.
The difficulty override is set, so the older difficulty offset is effectively ignored.
The server is PvE, but options that only matter on PvP servers are set.
The slot limit is set only in the INI; add the launch flag, which is the one the server honours.
A question mark in the chain parts, or a space in the admin password, breaks the travel chain: use the INI for those values.
The cluster id is the word default, so unrelated servers may appear in the travel list. Use a private random id.

presets.label: Official defaults
presets.description: The shipped rates: normal taming and experience, standard harvest and the built-in creature anchors.

presets.label: Boosted 2x
presets.description: Double experience, taming and harvest with faster breeding; the usual friendly boost.

presets.label: Boosted 5x breeding
presets.description: Normal rates with very fast hatching and maturing, for tribes that only want the breeding loop sped up.

presets.label: Hardcore PvE
presets.description: PvE with hardcore deaths, high difficulty and harsher survival drains.
